title: Polynomial-time tuple transformation
statement: Let $f$ be a polynomial-time computable function on bit strings, and let $\ell_1,\ell_2$ be functions from bit strings to nonnegative integers such that the unary words of lengths $\ell_1(y)$ and $\ell_2(y)$ are polynomial-time computable from $y$. For each $i\in\mathbb N$, the following transformation is polynomial-time computable: given $z$, set $s=\pi_1^{i+1}(z)$, where $\pi_1$ is the total first projection of the pair encoding; then apply the $i$-fold tuple decoder to $z$ using the base map $(s,w)\mapsto f(\pi_1(w),\operatorname{pad}(\pi_1(s),\pi_2(w)))$, decoder $(s,v)\mapsto\operatorname{pad}(\pi_2(s),v)$, and side word $\langle 1^{\ell_1(s)},1^{\ell_2(s)}\rangle$.
hypotheses_covered: The unary word of length $\ell_1(y)$ is polynomial-time computable for every input $y$
The unary word of length $\ell_2(y)$ is polynomial-time computable for every input $y$
